whisper.label: Whisper Large-V3
whisper.text: Chuck Paxton. I've been doing holography now for about 10 years. Basically taught myself in the garage with the use of just a $50 kit from a laser supply house. And got more information on it. Started to grow into holography in the garage. A couple years, I had the opportunity to meet Fred Entiser, who wrote the book I was currently using, and found he was teaching at Pasadena College. So, hooked up together, and he's done a lot to broaden my expertise in holography. In around 1991, Fred Entiser introduced me to one of his students, Roy Chirot, who was at the process of building a lab in an old wine cellar behind his house. We hooked up together and formed the Photon Cantina. From there, we basically started a business selling display holography to distributors for retail sale. This hologram we shot in 91, when we were with the Photon Cantina. This is a transmission hologram. It's our master we used for making the production of reflection holograms. Transmission master, we shot this one around the same time period as the Dolphins in 91. And I really like this one because it has the element of a magnifying glass. From the master, we put it back into setup and illuminated it with laser light, and actually projected an image out in space. Placed our H2, which was our transfer film, in that space, and we were able to capture that 3D image. This is my most recent hologram. I shot this in March of 2003. And the holograms of a 5,000 year old bronze from the Mesopotamian era. And I did this project for the professor of archaeology over at UCLA. Now this is the final transfer of the master we saw earlier, of just the lion. This is the lion of Yurkesh. It's like the 5,000 year old bronze. And what I've done here is, did a series of different shots. Different emulsion swellings. What we're looking at now is the composite stereogram table. We've got the laser here, transfer mirror to the beam splitter. Sends the first beam up through the spatial filter to the overhead mirror, and then down to our plate holder. Second beam comes through, through the film holder, which projects the image onto the diffuser. And the way I see it now is this is the way holography is going. This is the new change in holography. It's coming out of the going from computer to a holographic output.
